The standard deviation and the coefficient of variation decide. In this lesson: Calculate the standard deviation by the direct and assumed mean methods.
Calculate the coefficient of variation.
Use CV to compare consistency.

body.en: The *standard deviation* (σ) is the square root of the mean of the squared deviations from the arithmetic mean. Squaring removes the signs without ignoring them, so σ can be used in further algebra. It uses every value and is the most widely used measure of dispersion. Its square is the variance. For a frequency series, weight each squared deviation by its frequency. With an assumed mean A and d = x − A, σ = √(Σd²/N − (Σd/N)²), which avoids decimals.

points.en: Adding a constant to every value does not change σ
Multiplying every value by k multiplies σ by k

say.en: The standard deviation sigma is the square root of the mean of the squared deviations from the arithmetic mean. Squaring removes the signs without ignoring them, so sigma can be used in further algebra. It uses every value and is the most widely used measure of dispersion. Its square is the variance. For a frequency series, weight each squared deviation by its frequency. With an assumed mean A and d equals x - A, sigma equals the square root of (Σd squared/N - (Σd/N) squared), which avoids decimals. sigma equals the square root of (Σ(x - x̄) squared/N).
Shortcut: sigma equals the square root of (Σd squared/N - (Σd/N) squared).
Adding a constant to every value does not change sigma.
Multiplying every value by k multiplies sigma by k.

body.en: Karl Pearson's *coefficient of variation* expresses σ as a percentage of the mean: CV = σ/x̄ × 100. Because it is a pure number, it compares the variability of series with different means or units. The series with the smaller CV is more consistent, stable, uniform or homogeneous; the one with the larger CV is more variable.

points.en: Used to compare players, shares, crops and incomes

explanation.en: CV of P = 10/50 × 100 = 20%; CV of Q = 6/40 × 100 = 15%. Lower CV means more consistent, so Q is more consistent even though P scores more on average.

problem.en: The prices of a share over 5 days were ₹102, 98, 105, 95 and 100. Find σ by the assumed mean method with A = 100, and the CV.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. The prices of a share over 5 days were ₹102, 98, 105, 95 and 100. Find σ by the assumed mean method with A = 100, and the CV.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. The prices of a share over 5 days were 102, rupees 98, 105, 95 and 100. Find sigma by the assumed mean method with A equals 100, and the CV.
d equals x minus 100: 2, minus 2, 5, minus 5, 0; Σd equals 0.
d squared: 4, 4, 25, 25, 0; Σd squared equals 58.
sigma equals the square root of (58 over 5 minus 0 squared) equals the square root of 11.6 equals 3.41.
Mean equals 100 plus 0 over 5 equals 100; CV equals 3.41 over 100 times 100 equals 3.41 percent.
So the answer is sigma equals 3.41 rupees and CV equals 3.41 percent.

heading.en: SD ignores a shift, not a stretch

body.en: Add or subtract the same number from every value: σ stays the same. Multiply every value by k: σ is multiplied by |k|. That is why the assumed mean method works.
